title: Familiar letters, not related languages, let unseen languages into a shared space of meaning
abstract: arXiv:2611.06006v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Hundreds of languages have written text but almost no translations, and whether a model learning one from untranslated text builds on a related language or familiar letters is unclear: they usually coincide. Here we show that familiar letters, not a related language, let an unseen language into a shared space of meaning. GlyphMind, a tokenizer-free vision transformer that reads text as pixels and lets any sentence be shown in any script, was pretrained to align translations across 27 writing systems. Adapted on untranslated Lao, a language and script it had never seen, it retrieved English translations seven times as often as the strongest simple baseline. Rewritten in unfamiliar letters, Lao did not enter although its close relative Thai was in pretraining; Santali, which had none, entered in Devanagari, familiar from Hindi, but not in its own script. translated_title: 熟悉的字母，而非相关的语言，让未见过的语言进入共享的意义空间
translated_abstract: 数百种语言拥有书面文本却几乎没有翻译，而模型在从未翻译的文本中学习一种语言时，究竟是依托于相关语言还是熟悉的字母，目前尚不清楚：因为这两者通常同时出现。在此，我们证明了是熟悉的字母而非相关语言，让一种未见过的语言进入了共享的意义空间。GlyphMind 是一个无需分词器的视觉 Transformer，它将文本作为像素读取，并允许任意句子以任何文字系统呈现，其预训练目标是跨 27 种书写系统对齐翻译。在它从未见过的语言和文字——老挝语的未翻译文本上进行适配后，其检索英语翻译的成功率达到了最强简单基线的七倍。然而，当老挝语被改写成不熟悉的字母时，即使其近亲泰语已包含在预训练中，老挝语也未能进入共享空间；而桑塔利语在预训练中没有任何近亲语言，却借助印地语中熟悉的天城文进入了共享空间，用其自身文字则不行。因此，将文本转写为熟悉的书写系统，或许能让多语言模型向那些……（原文在此处截断）的语言开放。
tldr: 研究发现，决定从未见过的语言能否进入多语言模型共享语义空间的关键是“熟悉的文字系统”而非“相关的语言”——将没有翻译数据的语言转写成模型已熟悉的字母（如天城文），即可使其进入共享的意义空间。
en_tdlr: Familiar scripts—not related languages—let unseen languages enter a multilingual model's shared space of meaning, so transliterating low-resource languages into scripts the model already knows can unlock them.
